uncited: This family of methods incorporates probabilistic models into differentiable volume rendering to quantify aleatoric (data) and epistemic (model) uncertainty, or to enforce structural priors on the rendered output.

Unlike deterministic regularization losses that penalize deviations from a fixed target, these methods model the observation or scene distribution as a random variable, allowing the optimizer to downweight noisy observations or enforce sharp material boundaries [2961-uncertainty-prediction-loss.md][2964-uncertainty-aware-squared-error-loss.md][2274-beta-distribution-prior-on-exit-opacity.md].
They are distinguished from sibling methods by their explicit handling of variance parameters or distributional assumptions rather than simple geometric or photometric penalties.
All methods in this family extend the standard differentiable rendering pipeline by introducing additional network outputs or loss terms that depend on a probabilistic distribution.

The core mechanism involves predicting or optimizing a variance/uncertainty parameter alongside the scene representation (density, color, SDF) [2961-uncertainty-prediction-loss.md][2964-uncertainty-aware-squared-error-loss.md].

The optimization objective typically combines a data fidelity term weighted by the predicted uncertainty with a regularization term that prevents the uncertainty from collapsing to zero or exploding [2961-uncertainty-prediction-loss.md][2964-uncertainty-aware-squared-error-loss.md].
where $y_i$ is the ground truth, $\hat{y}_i$ is the prediction, and $\sigma_i^2$ is the predicted variance [2964-uncertainty-aware-squared-error-loss.md].

For structural priors, the method applies a probability density function (e.g., Beta distribution) to the final rendered values (such as exit opacity) to penalize intermediate values that represent ambiguous or noisy material [2274-beta-distribution-prior-on-exit-opacity.md].

The integration of uncertainty quantification into neural rendering addresses the limitations of deterministic point estimates, which often fail to communicate confidence in noisy or sparse data regimes.
